title: TCP/IP Model
homeDescription: Match the four TCP/IP Model layers to their definitions, then identify layers from descriptions.
studyGuideDescription: Practice matching TCP/IP Model layer definitions and identifying layers from descriptions.

tabs.label: [DEFINITIONS]
tabs.heading: [TCP_IP_DEFINITION_MATCHING]
tabs.description: Match each TCP/IP Model layer to its definition.

items.definition: The highest TCP/IP Model layer; consists of the OSI Application, Presentation, and Session layers.
The TCP/IP Model layer that consists of just the Transport layer of the OSI model.
The TCP/IP Model layer that consists of just the Network layer of OSI.
The lowest TCP/IP Model layer; consists of the Data-Link and Physical layers.

tabs.label: [DESCRIPTIONS]
tabs.heading: [TCP_IP_LAYER_IDENTIFICATION]
tabs.description: Identify the TCP/IP Model layer described by each clue. These descriptions do not use OSI layer names.

questions.prompt: Which TCP/IP Model layer provides network services directly to user applications, such as name resolution and web communication?
questions.explanation: The Application layer provides network services used directly by software applications.

questions.prompt: Which TCP/IP Model layer provides end-to-end delivery between applications and can manage reliability, sequencing, and flow control?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer manages communication between applications, including delivery controls such as reliability and flow control.

questions.prompt: Which TCP/IP Model layer uses logical addresses and routing to move packets between separate networks?
questions.explanation: The Internet layer handles logical addressing and routing packets between networks.

questions.prompt: Which TCP/IP Model layer handles local delivery over a network connection, including framing, hardware addressing, and access to the transmission medium?
questions.explanation: The Network Access layer handles local transmission, framing, hardware addressing, and access to the network medium.
